semantic_fragments.content: Verify the Design of the User Interface: Verify that the user interface design meets specified user interface requirements. Ensure that verifiable parameters are met without requiring usability tests. Design verification can be part of the product realization process and is essential for quality management.

User Interface Evaluation plan will be integrated into the overall Usability Engineering project plan. The plan is composed of Formative Evaluation (development and exploration) and Summative Evaluation (confirmation). The User Interface Evaluation activities are synchronized with other development tasks. As this is a mature device, one formative evaluation is conducted during design input stage, and one formative evaluation is conducted with prototype device followed by usability tests. This usability test is also a pre-summative evaluation, if it reveals findings that require design changes, new evaluation will be conducted on changed device. Design development engineer, customer representatives will participate the formative evaluation, usability test will be conducted on participants represent the end users.

Formative Evaluation Plan: (1) Objective: identify and address any usability issues in the user interface design of the Infrared Forehead Thermometer device to prevent potentially harmful use errors. (2) Timing and Frequency: Plan to conduct two Formative Evaluations throughout the design and development process. Conduct the initial Formative Evaluation during the design input stage to catch major design flaws. The second Formative Evaluation should be conducted during design validation stage, focusing on specific areas of improvement. (3) Evaluation Methods: expert reviews and cognitive walkthroughs in the early stage, and usability testing with representative users in the validation stage. (4) Evaluation Criteria: Assess ease of learning and use, efficiency, error rates, and user satisfaction. Identify specific use scenarios and critical tasks to evaluate in each Formative Evaluation.

Summative Evaluation Plan: (1) Objective: confirm the safety and effectiveness of the user interface design of the Infrared Forehead Thermometer device. (2) Test Design: Develop a Summative Evaluation plan based on regulatory requirements and guidelines for usability and human factors engineering. Define specific tasks and scenarios representing typical use cases and potential risks. Determine appropriate sample size of representative users. (3) Test Environment: Set up a controlled environment that mimics the intended use environment. Include appropriate equipment and support materials. (4) Evaluation Metrics: Define relevant metrics such as task success rates, error rates, and user satisfaction ratings. Establish acceptance criteria for each metric to determine if the user interface meets usability and safety requirements. (5) Analysis and Reporting: Analyze data to identify usability issues, use errors, or concerns related to device safety. Document findings and recommendations for design improvements or risk mitigation measures.

Summary of Formative Evaluations: This is a mature device; the previous generation has been marketed in the EU, and the device is for home use. There are two formative evaluations for this device: the first stage is during design input, the second stage is during device validation. In the design input stage, cognitive walkthroughs and interviews from experienced engineers and customer representatives were conducted. The formative evaluation in this stage is input of hazard and hazard situation identified in the risk assessment. The Infrared Forehead Thermometer's user interface has been refined to ensure safety, usability, and alignment with user needs before moving on to summative evaluation. In the design validation stage, usability test has been conducted on the finished device by representative operators.
